parties:
Bangladesh ------ Appellant 
vs.
Haji Mozaffaruddin ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Mr. Moazzem Hossain, the learned Deputy Attorney General has taken me through the pleadings, the judgments of the courts below and other relevant papers. He contends that even assuming the statements of the plaintiff made in the plaint that he could not catch fishes for the lease period due to the obstruction created by the Pak. Army and the local people before arid after the War of Liberation of Bangladesh, as correct he cannot claim any extension of lease and or injunction as prayed and granted by the courts below, as the appellant Government is not responsible for the loss or injuries, if any, sustained by the plaintiff-respondent, as the loss occurred due to war or vis major or Act of God. He also contends that under section 76 of the State Acquisition &Tenancy Act, the Government has got the exclusive right to settle the suit fisheries in the manner, they like and the court cannot grant any lease or extend the lease in the manner done by the impugned judgments. The relevant portion of section 76 of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act runs as follows: 

 10. In the present case, it is admitted that the respondent got the lease on auction as per the provision of rule 205(1) of the Estate Manual as quoted above. It is further admitted that the plaintiff was put in possession of the suit fisheries by the Government and there was no dispute about the title of the Government in the suit fisheries or any injunction from any court prohibiting the respondent rom post-that’s easing the suit fisheries. So, the principles laid down in rule 205 of the Estate Manual as referred to by the learned Munsif, is not applicable in the facts of the present case, which fact is also admitted by the learned Munsif. As already stated, the recommendation for giving further lease of the suit fisheries to the respondent for 3 years from 1378-81 B.S. was rejected due, to the change of laws and rules regarding the settlement of fisheries by Memo. No. 1M 3073/73/1219/(38) JM dated Dhaka 1st August, 1973. Thus, it is clear that no rule or law was violated by the Government in refusing the lease to the respondent in the manner alleged, as the Appellant Government is not bound by any law or rule in this respect to give further settlement of the suit fisheries to the respondent for the period from 1378-81 B.S. as claimed. The courts below also did not or could not cite any breach of contract, law, rule or privilege by the Appellant-Government in refusing the lease to the respondent The courts below passed the decree against the appellant as an equitable relief as he allegedly suffered loss for the period from 1376-78 B.S. for reasons stated above. Under section 76 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as quoted earlier, the Appellant Government has got the sole right to lease the suit fisheries in any manner it likes and the court has got no jurisdiction to entertain any application or suit covering any matter relating to the settlement.
